minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard the FY25 capital plan, kept its chair and vice chair, named a clerk and set liaisons.
minutes.summary: The town manager presented the preliminary FY25 capital plan, with the ten recommended projects and a ten-year outlook, and the committee questioned the Turkey Hill ADA study scope and the idea of a grant writer. The committee then reorganized, choosing a clerk, chair and vice chair, and assigned liaisons to town boards. It also discussed how to get school budget information earlier in budget season, and approved prior minutes.

public_comment.speaker_as_heard: on a lock with 91 Main Street
public_comment.topic: Thanked the committee for its work over the past year and for serving as a link between boards and day-to-day operations.
Objected to the earlier suggestion that a liaison's spouse sitting on a commission was a conflict of interest, noting other members serve on related bodies.

votes.motion: Nominate Tiffany Tarez as clerk of the finance committee.
Nominate Evan as chair and Chris as vice chair for the next term.
Approve the minutes with three changes: location, absent members, and correct spelling of a member's name.

budget_items.what_was_said: The generator bid came in within the appropriation. Surplus from completed projects will be transferred to cover a slight overage.
The state is announcing funding for fall storm costs from the supplemental budget, pending FEMA allocation. Lunenburg submitted expenses.
Thirty-five capital requests were prioritized for FY25, and the top ten are recommended.
Items included radio system, key card access, Northfield culvert, Turkey Hill ADA study, K9 and traffic cruisers, and security cameras.
The remaining projects are not recommended for funding.
The town manager recommends funding capital with free cash and unexpended capital this year and has earmarked free cash for stabilization and OPEB per policy.
Historical capital spending averages are well below ten-year requests, much of which relate to Turkey Hill and the town office building and would need borrowing.

budget_items.topic: Capital plan assumptions and special purpose stabilization
budget_items.what_was_said: Assumptions include raise-and-appropriate at a percent of the omnibus budget and free cash baseline. Special purpose stabilization draws are planned in several years and need a two-thirds vote.
A member asked that ARPA funds applied to capital be added to the historical capital spending sheet.
A member questioned spending on a surface patch rather than waiting for full renovation.
The town appropriates 100% first and is reimbursed around half through MSBA.
The town manager requested a 2.5% school increase while the initial school proposal was higher, a gap of over about six hundred thousand.

transfers.description: Surplus from completed projects to the generator project line to cover a slight overage

decisions.decision: Liaison assignments accepted by consensus without a formal vote; chair to post the list on SharePoint.
No meeting on January 25th; next meeting February 8th.

Town manager to send an updated budget calendar moving the school budget to the 21st, and the chair to request numbers early from department heads; the school committee chair and superintendent to be invited to February 8th.
The grant writer position to be discussed at a future meeting and considered for the committee report.
The Turkey Hill study line title to be taken back to the school committee for a possible clearer description before the warrant is printed.

what_happened.line: The town manager presented the preliminary FY25 capital plan: thirty-five requests were ranked and the top ten recommended, to be funded from free cash and unexpended capital.
The committee passed unanimously a nomination of a clerk, then a chair and vice chair for the next term.
Liaison assignments to town boards were accepted by consensus with no formal vote; the chair is to post the list on SharePoint.
Members asked for ARPA-funded capital to be added to the capital history sheet and questioned the Turkey Hill ADA study line and a grant writer position.
The town manager is to send a revised budget calendar moving the school budget to the 21st, and the school committee chair and superintendent are to be invited to February 8th.

why_it_matters: The capital plan decides which town projects, such as the radio system, culvert and Turkey Hill study, are put forward for funding, and the ten-year outlook flags larger items that would need borrowing and a town vote.

Getting the school budget numbers earlier in the cycle gives the committee more time to review the school appropriation, the largest part of the town's spending, before residents are asked to vote on it.
watch_next: February 8th meeting, with the school committee chair and superintendent invited and the updated budget calendar due from the town manager.
Whether the Turkey Hill study line title is changed before the warrant is printed.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main votes (clerk, chair, vice chair) and on the headline figures. Ours records far more of the capital discussion, and the official minutes add some follow-ups and a public commenter. The key difference is that the official minutes state no vote outcomes, so 'passed unanimously' and the consensus on liaisons rest on our recording alone. The top-ten capital project amounts and several action items also differ and need a check against the recording or capital plan.
